messages:
Priya: customer acct-447 seeing p95 spikes + occasional 502s on embeddings endpoint since ~2026-03-16 22:00 UTC. They captured a few request ids but we need a proper repro pack (prompt set, concurrency profile, token counts) + debug bundle. initial request ids: req:abc123, req:def456, req:ghi789. Can someone own collection?

Jordan: on it. Can you paste the raw curl for one of the failing requests (headers + body) or ask them to run a curl that includes X-Request-ID so we can map proxies? Also useful: client concurrency pattern (clients, rps per client, duration) and average prompt token counts.

Priya: sending what we have from the customer below — they ran an internal stress script but didn't capture per-request ids consistently. They can run a focused reproducer. Concurrency they used: 48 parallel clients, 5 RPS per client, 5m run. Promptset: 30 unique prompts; average prompt tokens ~240, avg completion tokens ~120. Attach sample prompt set: (we'll include in repro pack).

Maya (acct-447): confirming — here's the minimal curl we used to repro intermittently. Sometimes we get 200 w/ high latency, sometimes 502.

Maya (acct-447): ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwk-embed-2","input":"<prompt here>","max_tokens":256}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" --trace-ascii /tmp/curl-trace.txt
```

Jordan: perfect — ask them to include --trace-ascii and attach the trace files. Also ask them to run the curl with a static request-id header to make mapping easier: `-H 'X-Request-ID: test-repro-<index>'`. Example stress harness snippet I recommend they run locally or we can simulate: 

Jordan: ```
# stressplan.sh (example)
for i in $(seq 1 48); do 
  ./parallel-client --clients 1 --rps 5 --duration 300 --cmd "curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"X-Request-ID: repro-$i\" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" &
done
wait
```

Kevin: I'll pull infra logs for the window 2026-03-16 21:50 -> 22:10 UTC and correlate by request ids once we have the X-Request-ID values. Also need the pod names if you have them (or the customer can include the backend node id from trace).

Priya: customer ran one more short run and attached two new ids: req:jkL222, req:mno333. They said p95 jumped from ~450ms to ~1.2s under the same load. They can share the stress harness output (latency histogram) if helpful.

Jordan: good. Plan for reproducible pack:
- Prompt set: 30 prompts (already in thread)
- Token matrix: avg prompt 240 tokens, avg completion 120 tokens, peak prompt 1024 tokens (we should include a few edge-case prompts)
- Concurrency: 48 parallel clients, 5 rps each (ramp 0->5 in 30s), run 5 minutes
- Model variants to test: rwk-embed-2 (primary), rwk-embed-2-quant (fallback)
- Curl reproducer with X-Request-ID and --trace-ascii

Jordan: I'll assemble the repro pack (prompt set + payload.json + stress script + expected latency baseline) and run it against our staging cluster first. If we can reproduce, we'll collect a debug bundle and timeline.

OpsBot: debug-bundle job queued for window 2026-03-16T21:50:00Z -> 2026-03-16T22:10:00Z. Bundle ID: dbundle-20260316-777. Download at https://internal.redwood/debug/bundles/dbundle-20260316-777 (restricted).

Kevin: grabbed logs and started correlation for req:abc123, req:def456, req:ghi789, req:jkL222, req:mno333. Early signal: KV cache hit rate dropped during the spike window on node gpu-12 and we saw an OOM-kill on a worker at 2026-03-16T21:58:14Z. I'm pulling pod restarts and dmesg.

Priya: customer, can you run one targeted short run using the provided stressplan snippet but with only 6 clients and keep one of the prompt strings that produces long completions? That will help us isolate whether it's KV cache jitter vs pure compute saturation. If you can attach the curl traces (trace-ascii) and the stress harness stdout that would be ideal.

Maya (acct-447): will do — running now with 6 clients, will attach traces in this thread. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

Jordan: thanks all — action items: Kevin (collect infra-side artifacts + dmesg/pod events), Jordan (assemble repro pack + run on staging), Priya (coordinate with customer for focused runs and collect traces), OpsBot (provide debug bundle link). We'll reconvene in this thread when we have the customer's trace files and the staging run results.
